sections.h2: Where is the Monroe County Recorder of Deeds, and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The office is in the Administration Building at One Quaker Plaza, Room 106, in Stroudsburg. The main number is 570-517-3969. Doors open at 8:30 in the morning and close at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, with major holidays off.

Walk-in recording and title searches are available, though the county says appointments are strongly encouraged because space is limited. Packages can also arrive by post, or electronically through Simplifile, CSC and EPN. The county's record books start in 1836, the year Monroe County was formed from parts of Northampton and Pike counties, and anything recorded since August 1995 sits on its Landex system.

Beyond the recording fee itself, the office collects realty transfer tax for the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue and for every municipality and school district in the county. It also collects for the Monroe County Affordable Housing Agency, the Commonwealth Court Computer Automation fund, the Equal Access to Justice program and an archive fund for historical preservation of the land records.

The Recorder also runs a free Record Alert System, which sends a notice whenever a document is filed under the subscriber's name. An owner who wants to know about any filing against a property can sign up for it.

sections.h2: What are the Monroe County recording fees for a deed?
sections.html:
A deed or mortgage costs $87.75 under the fee bill that took effect November 17, 2025 and was revised the next day with no fee increase. The bill adds $2.00 for each page over four, $0.50 for each name over four, and $10.00 for each tax code number on a document.

Source: Monroe County Recorder of Deeds fee bill. Realty transfer tax is listed as 1 percent state and 1 percent local.

The bill spells out several payment rules. Personal checks are not accepted, the payment must be the exact amount because the office gives no change or refunds, and there is a $2.00 service charge on every rejected document. A stamped self-addressed envelope is required for the return of originals.

sections.h2: What must a Monroe County deed contain before the Recorder will accept it?
sections.html:
The county's answer is that the document must be an original, properly signed, dated and acknowledged before a notary, with the notary's seal, signature and expiration date. All recording fees and transfer taxes are due at the moment of recording.

  • A tax code number for the parcel.
  • A property description that names the municipality.
  • A transfer tax payment, or a Realty Transfer Tax Statement of Value filed in duplicate when the tax is not paid or the true value is not shown, as with a $1.00 deed.
  • A stamped, self-addressed return envelope.

The staff will not draft a deed. The county says its employees cannot and will not prepare deeds, and that a recorded deed cannot be altered, so changes such as adding a spouse or fixing an error go through a new deed or a deed of correction. Original deeds go back to the buyer, and mortgages go back to the lender.

sections.h2: How is realty transfer tax split when a Monroe County house sells?
sections.html:
The state share and the municipal share are 1 percent apiece, applied to the property's value, which the county warns can differ from the sale price. Contracts often split the bill between the two sides. Even so, a deed is turned away unless the tax is paid when it is presented, and the new owner carries the risk if the amount is questioned later.

The county's FAQ names the family exemptions: husband and wife, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and brothers and sisters, plus deeds between former spouses. Non-profit corporations get no break. State revenue guidance also exempts deeds to government units and property that passes by inheritance.

If state investigators decide a property is worth more than the stated value, or that an exemption was not valid, the Department of Revenue sends the owner a determination. The additional tax and interest go to the state, a matching municipal amount is paid at the recorder's office, and the deed is re-recorded for the usual fees.

sections.h2: What happens in Monroe County when property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent real estate taxes go to the Monroe County Tax Claim Bureau, which handles 20 municipalities and four school districts and receives about 9,000 delinquent returns a year. The bureau works under the Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act 542 of 1947, whose purpose is to return tax-delinquent properties to the productive tax rolls.

The bureau sits in Room 104 of the same Administration Building, at 570-517-3172, with hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Its page lists a lien certificate service, and a seller whose taxes are behind should ask for one so the closing agent knows what must be paid from proceeds. The bureau accepts money orders, cashier's checks and card payments at its counter, and repository sales are run through Bid4Assets.

A seller with delinquent taxes should contact the bureau before listing, since the amount owed will need to be settled as part of the sale.

sections.h2: What does the Pocono setting mean for a Monroe County seller?
sections.html:
Stroudsburg is the county seat of this Pocono county in northeast Pennsylvania, which the 2020 census put at 168,327 people. It borders Northampton County and the Lehigh Valley to the south, the Delaware River and New Jersey to the east, and Pike, Wayne, Carbon and Luzerne counties on its other sides. About 608 square miles are land.

The county grew fast in the late twentieth century as New York commuters and Pocono tourism arrived, and the 2020 census listed 79,114 housing units, 21.3 percent of them vacant. Owners held 76.6 percent of occupied homes.

Four school districts serve the county: East Stroudsburg Area, Pleasant Valley, Pocono Mountain and Stroudsburg Area. Interstates 80 and 380 are the main highways, and East Stroudsburg University anchors the town of the same name. Part of the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, a park of nearly 70,000 acres, lies inside the county, and the Appalachian Trail runs along its southern edge. The Monroe County Transit Authority, known locally as the Pocono Pony, runs fixed bus routes. The climate is humid continental, with hardiness zones running from 5a to 6b.

faqs.q: How much does the Monroe County Recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: The base fee is $87.75 for a deed or mortgage. Pages over four cost $2.00 each, names over four cost $0.50 each, and every tax code number on the document costs $10.00.

faqs.q: Does Monroe County accept personal checks for recording?
faqs.a: No. The fee bill rules out personal checks and requires the exact amount, with no change or refunds. Ask the office which payment forms it takes before sending a package.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Monroe County?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile, CSC and EPN are the three e-recording routes the county lists, and paper still works by post or at the Stroudsburg counter.

faqs.q: Who is exempt from transfer tax on a Monroe County sale?
faqs.a: Deeds among spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings are exempt, and so are deeds between ex-spouses. Non-profit corporations are not exempt. For any other case the county advises talking to an attorney.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent Monroe County real estate taxes?
faqs.a: Go to the Tax Claim Bureau in Room 104 at One Quaker Plaza, Stroudsburg. It takes money orders, cashier's checks and card payments in the office, and it can issue a lien certificate for a sale.
